summary: As humanity prepares for sustained exploration of the Moon and beyond, understanding how fires behave in microgravity is essential to protecting astronauts. Oxygen Runway addresses this challenge by transforming NASA's PSI-25 BASS-II dataset, containing 129 fire experiments conducted aboard the International Space Station, into an interactive scientific intelligence platform. Users can explore experimental conditions, investigate relationships between oxygen concentrations and other recorded variables, identify gaps in the available evidence, and generate customized fire-safety briefings. One particularly important finding is the gap between the dataset's highest recorded oxygen concentration of 22.2% and the 30% or higher oxygen environments that may be relevant to future lunar habitats. By making complex experimental data accessible, searchable, and easier to interpret, Oxygen Runway helps researchers and the public understand both what current evidence reveals and what questions remain unanswered about fire safety beyond Earth.
details:
Oxygen Runway is an interactive scientific data exploration and fire-safety decision-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's "Flame in Freefall" challenge. It transforms NASA's PSI-25 BASS-II dataset of 129 International Space Station microgravity fire experiments into an accessible environment for investigating combustion research.

How it works

The platform combines several interconnected features:

  • Interactive Oxygen Dial: Allows users to explore oxygen conditions and understand their significance in the context of microgravity fire research.
  • Experimental Data Explorer: Provides searchable, filterable scatterplots and tables through which users can examine individual experiments and recorded variables, including fuel samples, oxygen concentrations, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide measurements, and experimental conditions.
  • Evidence Coverage Heatmap: Highlights where experimental observations are available and where gaps remain in the dataset.
  • Individual Experiment Records: Lets users inspect the details of specific experiments rather than relying exclusively on aggregate statistics.
  • Make Your Brief Report: Generates customized fire-safety briefings based on user-selected conditions, incorporating relevant experimental records and nearest-test analysis. Reports can be downloaded or printed.
  • Data Analyst: Provides an interactive, browser-based interface for asking questions about the dataset and retrieving answers grounded in its recorded information.
  • CSV Export: Enables users to download experimental records for further investigation.

Why it matters

A major challenge for future space exploration is that fire behavior in microgravity and oxygen-enriched environments is not fully understood. Future lunar habitats may require oxygen concentrations of 30% or higher, yet the richest starting-air oxygen concentration represented in this dataset is only 22.2%. This creates an important evidence gap. Oxygen Runway makes that gap visible instead of extrapolating beyond what the experiments establish. It helps users distinguish documented observations from unanswered scientific questions, supporting more informed research into future spacecraft and lunar-habitat fire safety.

Technology and innovation

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Canvas and WebGL for interactive visual effects and SVG for scalable graphics. Experimental data is embedded locally, and the analytical features use browser-based JavaScript rather than requiring an external AI service or network connection. This makes the platform lightweight, accessible, and usable without depending on a live backend.

Oxygen Runway's creativity lies in bringing together scientific data exploration, evidence-gap analysis, and customized report generation in one cohesive mission-oriented experience. Rather than simply presenting NASA's data in charts, it gives users tools to investigate the experiments, understand the limitations of existing evidence, and communicate their findings through structured briefings.

What Makes Oxygen Runway Unique

Unlike conventional scientific dashboards that simply display experimental data, Oxygen Runway turns NASA's research into an interactive mission-control experience. Its distinctive interface combines a dynamic starfield, atmospheric visual effects, glowing telemetry elements, and an animated parchment-burning introduction to create an immersive environment inspired by spaceflight operations. However, its uniqueness extends beyond its visual design: every interface element is built around making complex scientific evidence easier to investigate and understand.

The platform's unique centerpiece is its "Make Your Brief Report" feature, which transforms user-selected experimental conditions into structured, evidence-based fire-safety briefings. Users can move beyond static charts through an interactive oxygen dial, explore individual experiments using searchable and filterable data visualizations, and use an evidence-coverage heatmap to identify underexplored experimental conditions. Its Data Analyst further enables natural-language-style exploration of the dataset, while CSV exports allow users to continue their analysis independently.

Most importantly, these features work together as a unified research workflow: users can explore experimental evidence, discover patterns, recognize limitations, and communicate findings through customized reports. Oxygen Runway makes scientific investigation feel less like reading a spreadsheet and more like operating a mission-intelligence system, bringing NASA's microgravity combustion research closer to researchers, students, and the public.
